 This Miscellaneous First Appeal is filed under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, praying to allow this appeal and set aside the judgment and award dated 31-01-2020 passed by the II Additional District and Sessions Judge and MACT, Kodagu-Madikeri, sitting at Virajpet, in M.V.C.No.22/2015 and consequently dismiss the claim petition in the interest of justice and equity; grant such other and further relief/s as this Court deems fit and proper under the facts and circumstances of the case, in the interest of justice and equity.
 This Miscellaneous First Appeal coming on for Admission,
through Physical Hearing/Video Conferencing, this day, the Court delivered the following:
JUDGMENT

The present appellant was one of the respondents in M.V.C.No.22/2015, in the Court of the II Additional District and Sessions Judge and MACT, Kodagu-Madikeri, Sitting at Virajpet (hereinafter for brevity referred to as "the Tribunal"), wherein the present respondent No.1 was the petitioner/claimant.

sentences.text: 2 The present respondent No.1, as the petitioner/claimant in M.V.C.N.22/2015 had filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter for brevity referred to as "the M.V. Act"), seeking compensation of a sum of `9,00,000/- towards the damages alleged to have been caused to the Motor Car bearing registration No.KA-04/MB-2712 in a road traffic accident said to have occurred on the date 11-11-2009 between the said Car and a KSRTC Bus bearing registration No.KA-09/F-3714.

The present respondent No.2, who was the respondent No.1 before the Tribunal, was alleged to be the driver of the said KSRTC Bus and the present appellant who was one of the respondents before the Tribunal was said to be the owner-cum-insurer of the alleged offending KSRTC Bus.
The compensation was sought from the second respondent before the Tribunal, which was the Managing Director of the KSRTC, Bangalore, along with the third respondent therein.

2. The contention of the claimant before the Tribunal was that, in the said road traffic accident,
which was said to have taken place on the date 11-11-2009, near Kalbetta Junction, Virajpet-Mysore Highway, the Motor Car bearing registration No.KA-04/MB-2712, said to have been driven by one Sri. Munavar Munna, i.e. the husband of the petitioner/claimant, had sustained total damages.

As such, in the said road traffic accident, the said husband of the petitioner, i.e. Sri. Munavar Munna is said to have sustained injuries and succumbed to the same, as such, the wife of the said deceased Munavar Munna has filed the claim petition before the Tribunal, for the damages said to have been caused to her Car, claiming a total compensation of a sum of `9,00,000/-.
3. Before the Tribunal, in response to the notice served upon them, all the respondents appeared through their counsels.
The Respondent No.2- KSRTC and Respondent No.4 - Insurer of the alleged Motor Car bearing registration No.KA-04/MB-2712 resisted the claim petition by filing their Written Statements.

The respondent No.2 denied the averments made regarding the manner of the occurrence of the accident and stated that the accident in question has not occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing registration No.KA-09/F-3714.
Respondent No.4 - Insurance Company denied that, both the drivers of the Motor vehicles had any valid Driving Licence as at the time of the accident.
It contended that the Motor Car was being driven by its driver without an effective and a valid driving Licence.
It denied that the petitioner/claimant is the owner of the said Motor Car.
It also contended that the claimant being the third party cannot claim compensation towards damages caused to the said Motor Car.
4. Before the Tribunal, the claimant got herself examined as PW-1 and got marked documents from Exs.P-1 to P-10.

On behalf of the respondents, neither any witness was examined nor any documents were got marked.
5.

After framing the issues and recording the evidence led by both side, the Tribunal, by its impugned judgment dated 31-01-2020, allowed the claim petition in part, holding the respondent KSRTC (appellant herein) before it, liable to pay the compensation to the claimant of a sum of `1,00,000/- together with interest thereupon at the rate of `9% per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of realisation of the amount.

The respondents No.2 and 3 before the Tribunal were jointly and severally held liable to pay the said compensation amount to the petitioner The Depot Manager Mysroe Rural Division vs Smt. Fathima Afsar on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188574666/
3 (claimant).

sentences.text: It is being aggrieved by the said judgment and award of the Tribunal, the said respondent - KSRTC, as the appellant has preferred the present appeal.
6. Records were called for from the Tribunal and the same are placed before the Court.
7. Learned counsel for appellant (KSRTC), learned counsel for Respondent No.1 (claimant) and learned counsel for respondent No.3 (Insurer) are appearing physically before the Court.
On a memo filed by the learned counsel for appellant, notice to Respondent No.2 (alleged driver of the offending KSRTC Bus) is dispensed with vide order dated 18-01-2023.
8. Though this appeal is posted at the stage of Admission, however, with the consent from the learned counsels for the parties, the same is taken up for its final disposal.
9. Heard the arguments from both side.

Perused the materials placed before this Court, including the memorandum of appeal, impugned judgment and also the records of the Tribunal.
10.

Learned counsel for the appellant (KSRTC) in her single sentence argument submitted that,
there is a delay of six years in filing the claim petition, as such, the petition ought not have been entertained and partly allowed by the Tribunal.
11.
Learned counsel for the respondent No.1 (claimant) submitted that, no grounds are made out to entertain the present appeal.

He further contended that the alleged delay in filing the claim petition has never been contended or canvassed by the present appellant before the Tribunal, in any manner,
at any stage.

Further, the learned counsels from both side submitted that, in respect of the very same road traffic accident, one more claim petition with respect to the death of the deceased Munavar Munna, the owner of the Motor Car bearing registration No.KA-04/MB-2712 and two separate claim petitions with respect to the injuries sustained by the two inmates in the said Motor Car in the very same accident was heard and decided by the same Tribunal, wherein the driver of the KSRTC Bus was held guilty of rash and negligent driving and it was the KSRTC that was held liable to pay the compensation.

12. Since from the very same accident, the present appeal has arisen, the question of the alleged rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing registration No.KA-09/F-3714 since has already been decided in the MFAs and the present appellant is also said to have satisfied the award in those appeals, the point of rash and negligent driving and the liability of the present appellant to pay the damages does not require a revisit by this Court.
13. The occurrence of the road traffic accident on the date as contended by the petitioner in her claim petition was further corroborated by her evidence as PW-1.

Apart from reiterating the contentions taken up by her in her claim petition, the petitioner also got produced and marked documents at Exs.P-1 to P-10, which inter alia includes copy of the FIR, copy of the death certificate,
copy of the R.C. Book, three photographs, copy of the The Depot Manager Mysroe Rural Division vs Smt. Fathima Afsar on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188574666/
4 - 10 - Insurance Policy, Motor Vehicle Inspector's Inspection Report.

sentences.text: In the cross-examination of PW-1, except making suggestions to the witness that there was negligent act on the part of the driver of the Motor Car itself, nothing more could be elicited from her evidence.
Thus, her evidence about the occurrence of the road traffic accident was not shaken.
On the contrary, the Police documents produced by her establishes that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the KSRTC Bus.

Added to the above, the submission of the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 and respondent No.3 also cannot be ignored that, arising out of the very same road traffic accident, three more claim petitions under Section 166 of the M.V. Act were instituted by the legal representatives of the deceased Munavar Munna and the two injured persons in the accident and that, all the three claim petitions came to be allowed.

In support of their contention, they have also produced a copy of the - 11 - judgment dated 26-07-2013 passed in M.V.C.Nos.141, 142 and 145 of 2010, in the Court of the Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Virajpet, a perusal of which would go to show that, with respect to the very same road traffic accident, three claim petitions, as contended by the learned counsels for respondents No.1 and 3 were filed and the said claim petitions came to be allowed, wherein it was held that the rash and negligent driving was solely on the part of the driver of the KSRTC Bus.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
According to the learned counsels for the said respondents, three Miscellaneous First Appeals filed against the said judgment before this Court in M.F.A.No.6796/2014,
M.F.A.No.6797/2014 and M.F.A.No.6798/2014 also came to be dismissed on the date 06-02-2017 by this Court.
The said submission has not been disputed or objected to by the learned counsel for the appellant - KSRTC.

Thus, apart from the evidence of PW-1, corroborated with the documentary evidence from Exhibits P-1 to P-10, the fact that with respect to the very same road traffic accident,
three more claim petitions - 12 - came to be allowed with respect to the death of a person and injuries caused to two inmates of the Car, wherein the driver of the offending KSRTC Bus was held solely liable for causing the road traffic accident, has not only stood established but also has remained undisputed.
Thus, the only ground taken up in the memorandum of appeal by the appellant-KSRTC alleging the non-negligence on the part of the driver of the KSRTC Bus, is not acceptable.
14. The other aspect which the appellant -KSRTC has taken in its memorandum of appeal is with regard to the quantification of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
It is contended that the quantification of the compensation at a sum of `1,00,000/- for the damages caused to the alleged Motor Car of the claimant is on the higher side.
It is also contended that there were no documents to show the payment made towards the repair charges of the Motor Car.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A perusal of the evidence led by PW-1 corroborated with the Motor Vehicle Accident report at - 13 - Ex.P-6 and three photographs at Ex.P-4 pertaining to the road traffic accident would clearly go to show that, the said Car was smashed to a considerable extent and was appearing to be a smashed junk of steel.
Thus, by looking at the photographs and the Motor Vehicle Accident report, it would clearly go to show that, the motor Car in the accident had sustained considerable damages.
16. Exs.P-8 and P-9 are the two tax invoices which have given the estimation for taking up the repairs of the Motor Car.
The petitioner has not produced the stamp receipt for having paid the said amount,
The evidence of PW-1 corroborated with the documentary evidence produced by the claimant, more particularly, Exs.P-8 and P-9 cannot be ignored or discarded.
Thus, it is considering all these aspects, the Tribunal has awarded a compensation of a sum of `1,00,000/- to the extensive damage caused to the Motor Car.

In the said process, the Tribunal has rightly observed that, when the Car itself was purchased for a sum of `2,00,000/-, it's total estimation - 14 - amount cannot be a sum of `2,80,757/-, as such, taking stock of the total circumstances of the case,
it has awarded a reasonable compensation of a sum of `1,00,000/- towards damages caused to the said Motor Car in the road traffic accident in question.
17. Lastly, though the learned counsel for the appellant - KSRTC has forwarded only one sentence argument, contending that there is a delay of six years in filing the claim petition

, however,
admittedly, there is no such stand taken up by the present appellant - KSRTC, as respondents before the Tribunal.
As such, for the first time, the alleged contention of delay in filing the claim petition has been taken up by the appellant- KSRTC.

In that regard, when the Court specifically asked the learned counsel for the appellant as to whether such a contention was taken up before the Tribunal at the first instance, and whether the said aspect was considered by the claims Tribunal, the learned counsel for the appellant, even after taking enormous time and when the Court was - 15 - repeatedly repeating the said question, anticipating the answer, did not answer to the said question.

18. In the light of the above, even the alleged delay has not been raised by the contesting respondents before the Tribunal at the appropriate time and in an appropriate manner and also in the absence of any such plea being taken even in the memorandum of appeal before this Court also,
a single sentence argument, which is the sole argument of the appellant -KSRTC, canvassing the alleged delay, cannot be accepted.

As such, I do not find any infirmity in the impugned judgment,
warranting interference at the hands of this Court.
